parsed_tool.name: GAPPA graft
parsed_tool.description: place query sequences as leaves on a reference tree

inputs.name: jplace
inputs.label: Phylogenetic placements (jplace JSON)
inputs.help: Placements from EPA-ng, pplacer, or another program producing the jplace format.

inputs.name: fully_resolve
inputs.label: Resolve each query as an individual branch
inputs.help: Disabled: queries on one reference branch are collected in a subtree. Enabled: place each query using its individual distal/proximal length.

inputs.name: newick_tree_quote_invalid_chars
inputs.label: Quote labels containing invalid Newick characters
inputs.help: Disabled: spaces and the characters :;()[],{} in node labels are replaced by underscores. Enabled: such labels are kept unchanged and put in quotation marks.

help.content:
Add placed query sequences as leaves to the reference phylogeny stored in a **jplace JSON** dataset from EPA-ng or pplacer.

The result is a Newick tree containing reference and query leaf names. GAPPA selects the most likely placement for each query, so the tree presents one position per query even when the input retains multiple candidate placements. Keep the original jplace data when interpreting placement uncertainty.

By default, queries placed on the same reference edge are grouped in a subtree attached to that edge. Enable **fully resolve** to insert queries individually at their placement positions along the edge. This changes the displayed topology; it does not estimate a new reference phylogeny, realign sequences or recalculate placement likelihoods.

Node labels containing spaces or the characters `:;()[],{}` are invalid in Newick. By default these characters are replaced by underscores, which most downstream tools accept. Enable **quote labels** to keep the original labels in quotation marks instead.

Use the Newick output for downstream tree analysis or visualization. Query and reference identifiers are retained for joining with abundance or annotation tables.
